# Context: types (dtype, Dtyped + derive, dimensions, ElementType, errors, crate root)

## Purpose

Runtime element-type descriptors (`Dtype`: scalar kind or struct of (name, offset, Dtype) fields,
plus an inner shape of <= 4 dims, `Itemsize = u16`, `Alignment` = power of two <= 32768), the
`unsafe trait Dtyped` that ties a Rust type to its `Dtype`, the `#[derive(Dtyped)]` proc macro,
the compile-time element tag (`Ty<T>` / `TypeDyn`), shape-argument plumbing (`Dimension`,
`Dim<N>`, `DimDyn`, `IntoDimension`, `DimArray`), and the error/validation helpers in `error.rs`.
Every reinterpretation of bytes as `T` elsewhere in the library is justified by a `Dtype`
equality check made here, and every struct-field view trusts the field offsets validated here.

## Contracts

Provided by this subsystem (what consumers rely on):

- C1. Every constructible `Dtype` (from `new_scalar`, `from_fields`, `new_struct`, `set_shape`,
  `T::DTYPE`) satisfies: `itemsize == base_itemsize * prod(shape)`; for structs every field lies
  in `[offset, offset + field.itemsize) subset of [0, base_itemsize)`, fields are in increasing
  offset order and non-overlapping, layout is exactly C-aligned or C-packed
  (`is_aligned_struct` dtype.rs:653-688 / `is_packed_struct` dtype.rs:691-717); `alignment` is
  max field alignment (aligned) or 1 (packed). `ops/sub_dtype.rs:124-152` relies on the field-in-
  bounds part with NO re-check (`unsafe with_offset`, `get_unchecked`, NdCopier over
  field.itemsize bytes). This invariant is only as good as the u16 arithmetic in the checks
  (see Suspicions S1).
- C2. `Dtype: PartialEq` (dtype.rs:914-941) compares itemsize, alignment, shape, then scalar kind or
  fields positionally (name, offset, nested Dtype recursively). It does NOT compare `is_aligned`.
  Equality is the gate for all safe reinterpretation: `check_dtype` (error.rs:153-167) ->
  `Ty<T>::from_dtype` (element_type.rs:81-84) -> `IntoType::new` (ops/into_type.rs:58-61), after
  which `IntoType::read_data` does `assert_unchecked_eq!(inner.dtype(), ET::DTYPE)`
  (ops/into_type.rs:87,102) - i.e. it also relies on `inner.dtype()` never changing.
- C3. `try_to_scalar()` (dtype.rs:822-825) is Some only for an exact scalar (empty inner shape);
  `scalar_kind()` (dtype.rs:724-729) is Some even with an inner shape (documented at 719-722).
- C4. `Alignment::as_usize()` is always a non-zero power of two <= 32768 (enum-backed, dtype.rs:41-96).
- C5. `DimDyn`/`DimArray` hold <= NDIM_MAX (8) entries; `Dim<N>::from_fn/vec` panic unless ndim == N
  (dimension.rs:261-285, error.rs:131-151); `IntoDimension` for slices/IxDyn returns
  `TooManyDimensions` instead of panicking (dimension.rs:395-403, 499-509).
- C6. `check_get_buffer_size` (error.rs:240-267) returns Ok only if `buf.len()` equals
  prod(range lens) * itemsize. This is the ONLY safety justification for
  `StridedBuf::from_slice_mut` in the safe `Array::to_ndarray_slice` (array.rs:840-853).
- C7. `check_get_range` (error.rs:211-230): ndim equal, `start <= end <= dim` per dim.
  `check_shape_overflow` (error.rs:185-200): prod(shape) * itemsize fits u64 (NOT usize).
  `check_dtype_size_nonzero` (error.rs:169-183): arrays of itemsize-0 dtypes are rejected (called by
  ArrayParams storage/params.rs:307, map/op1/op2/reduction/sub_dtype constructors).

Relied on by this subsystem / the implicit `Dtyped` contract (dtype.rs:1147-1155). The written
Safety text only says "matching the type size, alignment and inner fields". What the rest of the
library actually assumes of `unsafe impl Dtyped for T` (implementer is responsible; for derived
types the macro is):
- D1. `T::DTYPE.itemsize() as usize == size_of::<T>()` (storage/plain.rs:285-289 builds byte strides
  from `size_of::<T>()`; cast_slice users).
- D2. `T::DTYPE.alignment() == align_of::<T>()` (nd_copy.rs:90 debug_assert; derive asserts it at
  jix-macros/src/lib.rs:221). Violated by the built-in 8-byte scalar impls on i686 Linux (S3).
- D3. Field offsets / field dtypes equal the real Rust layout (SubDtype + `Ty<FieldT>`).
- D4. Every byte pattern that can reach a `T` buffer is a valid `T`. Unstated; false for `bool`
  (only 0/1) and any struct with a bool field. ops/transmute.rs:1-60 is `unsafe` precisely because
  of this, but decode/into_typed paths do not validate (S4).
- D5. Reading `T` as bytes assumes all bytes initialized; padded repr(C) structs are explicitly
  supported (dtype.rs:188-198) so their padding is read as `u8` by encode paths (theoretical UB).
- `Dtyped: Copy + Send + Sync + Sized + 'static` (Copy excludes Drop).
- `Dtype::new_struct_borrowed_unchecked` (dtype.rs:631-645, `pub`, `#[doc(hidden)]`,
  `const unsafe`): NO `# Safety` doc. Implicit precondition: (fields, itemsize, alignment,
  is_aligned) satisfy C1. Only caller: the derive (jix-macros/src/lib.rs:213-218). The macro does
  NOT re-run `is_aligned_struct`; it only asserts total size and align against Rust.
- `ElementType` (element_type.rs:16-31) is a pub, SAFE, unsealed trait, but unsafe code trusts
  `ET::DTYPE`, `from_dtype` and `dtype()` (S6). `Dimension` is effectively sealed via the
  `pub(crate) DimVec` bound on `type Vec<T>` (dimension.rs:74-78, 130-151).
- `ArrayVec` invariant `len <= CAP` (util/arrayvec.rs; `set_len` only debug_asserts, line 184).

## Unsafe inventory

- dtype.rs:75-77 `transmute::<u16, AlignmentInner>` - guarded locally by `1 <= v <= 32768 &&
  is_power_of_two` (line 72); every power of two in range is a variant. Sound.
- dtype.rs:93 `assert_unchecked(align != 0 && pow2)` - established by enum validity. Sound.
- dtype.rs:631-645 `new_struct_borrowed_unchecked` - see Contracts; justification is NON-LOCAL
  (proc-macro computation in another crate).
- dtype.rs:1101-1102 `ManuallyDrop::drop` in `OwnedFields::drop` - dropped once. Sound.
- dtype.rs:1160-1184 `unsafe impl Dtyped` for i8..u64, f32, f64, bool, `half::f16` (repr
  transparent u16, feature `half`), `num_complex::Complex<f32/f64>` (repr(C) re,im, feature
  `num-complex`). Relies on D1-D4; D2 fails on i686 Linux for I64/U64/F64/ComplexF64; D4 fails
  for bool unless every producer guarantees 0/1.
- dtype.rs:1186-1198 `unsafe impl<T: Dtyped, const N> Dtyped for [T; N]` - Rust array layout;
  const-eval asserts `N < 65535`, `insert_first_const` panics (compile error) if inner shape would
  exceed 4 dims, `itemsize *= n` overflow is a const-eval error. Does NOT check the shape product
  fits u16 when T is zero-sized (shape [300, 300] of an empty struct is constructible).
- dimension.rs:173,179 `assert_unchecked(len <= NDIM_MAX)` - relies on ArrayVec<_, 8> invariant
  (non-local; `set_len` callers).
- jix-macros/src/lib.rs:213 generated `unsafe { new_struct_borrowed_unchecked(..) }` and
  lib.rs:258 generated `unsafe impl Dtyped` - justification = macro layout computation +
  const asserts at 220-221 (named) / 244-245 (transparent). Non-local, see Hot spots.
- No unsafe in element_type.rs, error.rs, lib.rs; but error.rs:240-267 and element_type.rs feed
  `unsafe` elsewhere (C2, C6).

## Edge-case surface

- Struct layout detection: `from_fields` sorts by offset (stable, line 470) then tries aligned
  then packed; `new_struct` keeps caller order and requires monotone offsets, plus explicit
  itemsize/alignment. Both reject gaps, overlaps, trailing padding beyond C rules.
- Zero fields: `from_fields(vec![])` / derive on `struct S {}` -> itemsize 0, alignment 1,
  is_aligned. Zero-sized fields at the same offset as the next field are allowed (test
  `zero_size_field_does_not_affect_parent_layout`).
- `[T; 0]`: shape [0], itemsize 0, alignment of T (dtype.rs:1866 test). Every runtime
  constructor (`new_struct` 594-598, `set_shape` 852-856, from_proto) rejects a 0 dim, so such
  dtypes are only reachable from Rust types (S7). `set_shape` refuses a current zero-element shape
  (861-866).
- Itemsize u16: max 65535 bytes per element incl. inner shape; offsets are u16; all layout sums in
  dtype.rs are UNCHECKED u16 adds (S1). Max dtype alignment reachable via safe constructors is 8
  (struct alignment must equal a field max); larger only via manual `unsafe impl`.
- Inner shape: <= DTYPE_MAX_NDIM = 4 (`DtypeShape::from_slice` returns None); archive from_proto
  first checks `<= NDIM_MAX` (8) then relies on set_shape/new_struct for the 4 limit.
  `[T; N]` prepends N; `set_shape` replaces the whole shape.
- bool: 1 byte, alignment 1, valid values 0/1 only (doc dtype.rs:338); no decode-time validation.
- f16 / Complex: `ScalarKind::F16/ComplexF32/ComplexF64` always exist (archives/Python can carry
  them) even when the `half`/`num-complex` features are off; only the `Dtyped` impls are gated.
  ComplexF32 alignment is 4, ComplexF64 is 8 (hardcoded, dtype.rs:967-985).
- 32-bit targets (x86 = i686 Linux glibc+musl and Windows, armv7 wheels in release.yaml):
  `align_of::<u64/i64/f64>() == 4` on i686 Linux (8 on Windows i686 and armv7) vs hardcoded 8;
  `u64 as usize` truncation in error.rs:246-247; `DimDyn -> IxDyn` uses `try_into().unwrap()`
  (dimension.rs:215, 309) -> panic for dims >= 2^32. No 32-bit target is tested in CI.
- NDIM_MAX = 8: `Dim<7>`/`Dim<8>` map to `ndarray::IxDyn` (dimension.rs:338-339); ndarray
  `Dim<[usize; 7|8]>` has no `IntoDimension` (497-498). ndim 0 (`()`, `[u64; 0]`) is valid.
- Recursion: Dtype clone/eq/Debug/drop and from_proto recurse over nested structs; depth is bounded
  only by protobuf decode recursion limit.

## Intentional behaviors

- Only C-aligned or C-packed struct layouts; arbitrary NumPy offsets/gaps/overlaps are rejected
  (dtype.rs:273-274, 807). Not a bug that NumPy accepts more.
- Ambiguous offsets resolve to aligned in `from_fields` (doc dtype.rs:412-415, 561-565; test
  `from_fields_ambiguous_i32_u8_detected_as_aligned` dtype.rs:1418). Use `new_struct` to force.
- `from_fields` sorts fields by offset (test `from_fields_sorts_by_offset` dtype.rs:1432) and rejects
  duplicate names (460-467).
- Struct never equals a scalar of the same layout (test dtype.rs:1302); `[T; 1]` keeps shape [1],
  it is not the scalar T (test `array_size_1_has_shape` dtype.rs:1373).
- Zero-sized dtypes exist as dtypes but arrays of them are rejected (commit be18f6b; error.rs:169-183;
  tests dtype.rs:1829-1899).
- Little-endian only, compile-time assert (dtype.rs:390-395); big-endian archives rejected.
- Alignment capped at 32768 (dtype.rs:66-72); itemsize capped at u16::MAX (dtype.rs:271-272).
- Derive: generic named-field structs do not compile (documented jix-macros/tests/derive_external.rs:
  183-185); only `#[repr(transparent)]` single-field tuple structs may be generic; enums, unions,
  unit structs, `repr(C, align(N))`, `repr(packed(N))` are rejected.
- Arithmetic error defaults deviate from NumPy: DivideByZero and InvalidOperation = Error,
  Overflow and Underflow = Warn (error.rs:359-368; documented codec/mod.rs:418-421 and
  jix-py/src/error.rs:51). Integer x/0 yields 0 plus the flag (error.rs:384). Warnings are deduped by
  message (error.rs:340); in Error mode the first kind in order DivideByZero, Overflow, Underflow,
  InvalidOperation is raised (error.rs:326-346).
- `scalar_kind()` ignoring inner shape is documented (dtype.rs:719-722).

### Changed in c009869 (#87) - supersedes conflicting statements above (line numbers above refer to bb1ee2c)
- `check_shape_overflow` caps dims at i64::MAX; `check_region_size` bounds 32-bit read regions.
- jix-py's dtype_from_numpy debug_assert is relaxed for packed structs of 1-byte-aligned fields;
  big-endian numpy dtypes are rejected with an error.

### Changed in 6f8e220 (#88) and 7e93487 (#89) - supersedes conflicting statements above
- #88: struct dtypes cannot contain padding. `check_no_padding` (checked adds) requires fields to
  tile the element back to back, and `#[derive(Dtyped)]` rejects padded structs at compile time
  (K3, K42 fixed). dtype.rs was largely rewritten (~430 lines): re-read it.
- #89: the boolean element type is `jix::scalar::bool8` (jix/src/scalar/bool.rs, repr(transparent)
  u8, 0 = false, any other byte = true); `bool` is no longer `Dtyped`. Every Dtyped type must accept
  every bit pattern. The archive dtype proto changed for it.

### Changed in 4d11918 (#90) - supersedes conflicting statements above
- `Dtype::new_struct` rejects duplicate field names (K52). `[T; 0]` and arrays of zero-sized types
  are not `Dtyped` (K53). dtype.rs changed ~90 lines.

### Changed in 691e11b (#91) - supersedes conflicting statements above
- `Dtype::from_fields` computes the itemsize with `saturating_add` before `check_fields`, so an
  oversized field list returns Err in debug builds too (K83).
- `ElementType` is sealed (K70).
- `Idx::ceil_to_multiple` / `Idx::div_ceil` are gone; the derive macro and the crate use std
  `next_multiple_of` (in the derive it runs in const eval, so an overflow is a compile error).

## Hot spots

- Layout arithmetic in dtype.rs:476-506 and 653-717: every `expected_offset += itemsize` and
  `ceil_to_multiple` is unchecked u16 (`Idx::ceil_to_multiple` util/mod.rs:64-67 is
  `div_ceil(m) * m` with only a debug_assert). Can a crafted archive (conversions.rs:84-114 ->
  `new_struct`) or Python dtype pass validation with fields beyond itemsize in a release build?
  Python checks numpy itemsize fits u16 first (jix-py/src/dtype.rs:120-126), archives do not
  bound the field sum.
- Derive soundness (jix-macros/src/lib.rs): offsets are recomputed from `align_of`/`size_of` and
  declaration order, never checked with `offset_of!`; only total size/align are asserted. Is that
  enough for `repr(C)` (yes, C algorithm), bare `repr(packed)` (Rust repr - field order
  unspecified), i686 (uses `align_of`, while the Dtype validators use `F::DTYPE.alignment()`)?
  Does a field whose `DTYPE.itemsize != size_of` (manual impl) get caught? (No per-field check.)
- Hygiene of generated code: unqualified `size_of`, `align_of`, `assert!`, `std::borrow::Cow`
  (lib.rs:185,190,193,203,220-221,244-245) and block-local `BASE_OFFSET`/`FIELDS`/`ceil_to_multiple`
  resolve at the call site, so a user item with those names changes the computed layout or the
  checks without the user writing `unsafe`.
- `PartialEq` as the reinterpretation gate: can two dtypes compare equal and differ in layout?
  (is_aligned is ignored; it only matters for all-align-1 structs where layouts coincide, and for
  the numpy `align=` flag in jix-py/src/dtype.rs:58-71.) Can derive and from_fields/new_struct give
  different dtypes for the same Rust type (i686, packed with align-1 fields)?
- Producers of bool bytes: archive decode, numpy import, Plain over user memory, SubDtype of a bool
  field, Transmute. Who guarantees 0/1 before a `Ty<bool>` view or kernel reads it?
- `ElementType` trust (S6) and `ArrayStorage::dtype()` stability under `assert_unchecked_eq!`.
- error.rs:240-267 on 32-bit: `product::<u64>()` unchecked, `as usize` truncation, `nitems *
  itemsize` usize overflow, feeding `from_slice_mut` (array.rs:848-851).
- Recent churn (`git log -- <files>`): 98b2ed3 / 4645124 added ArithmeticOpStatus + error modes
  (error.rs:269-419, young code); 75fd25b removed the `D: Dimension` generic (dimension.rs reshaped);
  be18f6b "fail on itemsize=0, fix Dtyped macro bugs" (is_aligned flag was inverted in the derive
  before; zero-element set_shape fix). Previously-buggy areas are worth a second look.

### Suspicions (unverified)

- S1. dtype.rs:481,500,673,704 (and ceil at 479,492,671,682) - unchecked u16 adds wrap in release:
  e.g. `new_struct([a: u8[65535]@0, b: u8@65535, c: u8@0], [], itemsize 1, align 1)` passes
  `is_aligned_struct` (65535+1 wraps to 0), giving itemsize 1 with a 65535-byte field; reachable from
  a crafted .jix via conversions.rs:113; then `dtype_sub_field_dyn("a")` reads OOB in
  sub_dtype.rs:135/149-160. Debug builds panic instead of returning InvalidArchive.
- S2. jix-macros/src/lib.rs:115 - bare `#[repr(packed)]` is `repr(Rust, packed)` whose field order is
  not guaranteed (clippy `repr_packed_without_abi`, allowed in derive_external.rs:76); the macro
  assumes declaration order and never checks `offset_of!`, so FIELDS offsets may not match.
- S3. dtype.rs:967-985 - ScalarKind alignment hardcoded 8 for I64/U64/F64/ComplexF64 but
  `align_of` is 4 on i686 Linux (shipped x86 wheels): derived `#[repr(C)] {a: u32, b: f64}` gets
  b@4/align 4 with a field dtype of align 8, which `new_struct` rejects -> archives written there
  cannot be read back; nd_copy.rs:90 debug_assert fails; jix-py/src/dtype.rs:78-86 layout check
  may reject f8/c16 numpy conversions (numpy reports alignment 4 there).
- S4. dtype.rs:1184 (bool impl) + archive/numpy decode - no 0/1 validation on safe paths
  (`read_from_file(..).into_typed::<bool>()`, struct dtypes with bool fields), while
  ops/transmute.rs treats the same reinterpretation as unsafe.
- S5. error.rs:246-247 - on 32-bit, `as usize` truncation / `nitems * itemsize` wrap lets a too-small
  `buf` pass the size check in the safe `to_ndarray_slice` (array.rs:848-851), e.g. a broadcast u8
  array of shape [65536, 65537] read into a 65536-byte buf.
- S6. element_type.rs:16 - `ElementType` is a public safe trait; a user impl whose `DTYPE`,
  `from_dtype` or `dtype()` lie drives `assert_unchecked_eq!` (ops/into_type.rs:87,102) and SubDtype
  copies (sub_dtype.rs:91-99,154) into UB from safe code.
- S7. dtype.rs:1186-1197 vs conversions.rs:124-126 - a derived struct with a `[T; 0]` field has
  non-zero itemsize so it can be written, but to_proto emits shape [0] which from_proto rejects:
  write then read round-trip fails.
- S8. dtype.rs:578-629 - `new_struct` (used by archive and numpy paths) does not reject duplicate
  field names, unlike `from_fields`; SubDtype silently takes the first match.
- S9. dtype.rs:857 - `product::<Itemsize>()` unchecked in `set_shape`; `[[[Empty; 300]; 300]]`-style
  zero-sized dtypes have a shape product > u16 (the `[T; N]` impl never checks it) -> debug panic.
